reviews.reason: The supplier now permits reuse of covered demonstration labels. This procedure still explicitly requests an interactive expert and queries each visited state; that admissible algorithm is unchanged. Per-decision mixing, aggregation with multiplicity, attained-minimizer selector and finite output remain well defined.

The coverage caveat leaves this explicit uncovered-state witness sound: expert occupancy is concentrated at g, while a learner error reaches absorbing b. The recurrence gives cost sum(1-(1-epsilon)^k); the elementary upper and lower estimates hold also for T=1. All four TikZ transitions, directions and action/cost labels agree with the model.

Here expert-only rollouts really never visit b, so the supplier coverage caveat does not invalidate the missing-label assertion. The bad rollout visits g,b, losses 2 versus 0 select the good policy, and later g labels preserve the unique minimizer. The TikZ initial arrow and all four transition labels/directions match these deterministic transitions.

The first input clause incorporates the data/operators and admissible trial functions of the repaired loss definition, hence its measurable-singleton requirement applies in d=1. The d=1 branch additionally supplies each singleton mass and returns that exact finite weighted boundary sum. No independent assertion admits a nonmeasurable singleton; thresholds and finite empirical evaluations are unaffected.

The PINN citations provide optimizer context, while the actual witness is the scalar polynomial J=(theta^2-1)^2. Its derivative is 4 theta(theta^2-1), zero initialization remains zero, and the global zeros are exactly plus/minus one. No boundary measure or singleton mass is used, so the supplier repair has no mathematical effect.

The sine residual vanishes on j/m and its square integrates to 1/2 under uniform interior measure. Both endpoint residuals are zero; the exact boundary term is therefore zero for every admissible boundary probability measure in the supplier's repaired d=1 regime. The example neither assigns an undefined singleton mass nor asserts minimization of the regularized loss.

The strengthened definition requires properness as well as uniqueness of equality. This proof already establishes both: the logarithmic support argument gives nonnegative excess risk and treats q_j=0, while Brier excess risk is sum_i(q_i-p_i)^2. Truthful logarithmic risk remains finite on the simplex boundary. No equality-only inference is used.

The algorithm evaluates logarithmic loss, whose formula is unchanged by the definition repair, over a nonempty finite positive-temperature set. Finite logits make every softmax coordinate positive and validation loss finite; the smallest minimizer therefore exists. Its strict-propriety reference is supported by the explicit inequality proof, and the algorithm asserts no finite-sample calibration guarantee.

The supplier is used for simplex forecasts and the final comparison with log/Brier loss. Both losses satisfy the repaired proper-plus-equality definition by the cited theorem. The ECE/MCE formulas use only nonempty bins; a nonempty sample ensures the maximum has a nonempty finite index set. No equality-only characterization of strict propriety occurs.

The Statement assumes the nondivergence expression itself, with bounded continuous coefficients and nonpositive potential. Its exponential barrier uses precisely that expression, without differentiating arbitrary divergence-form coefficients. Thus the supplier's newly restricted classical flux domain invalidates no step. The maximum contradiction and the difference-function estimate retain the positive principal-part sign.

The actual operator is the smooth constant-coefficient Laplacian, so the repaired classical flux domain contains the constructed C-infinity interior solution. The convex sector has exterior tangent balls; the supplied cutoff makes the forcing smooth away from the vertex and zero near it. The radial second derivative grows as r^(-1/2), excluding bounded global C2alpha, and zero-boundary harmonic uniqueness still applies.

The inputs already call p_t the marginal densities of the specified X and require the exact marginal score and actual terminal law P_T. Hence the supplier's explicit marginal-density hypothesis holds, including after the stated time shift. The reverse drift has the required divergence term and positive score sign; one Euler predictor and one Langevin corrector make no exactness/convergence claim. Full AC remains explicit.
